summary: Patricia Fister specializes in Japanology, history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. She earned her Ph.D. from the University of Kansas (~1976–1983) and held posts at the University of Kansas (1984), Hakuho Women's College (1998), and the International Research Center for Japanese Studies (1991–2019).

Patricia Schiaffini-Vedani is a scholar of Sinology and Tibetology. She completed graduate studies at Peking University (1990–1994) under Zhao Zumo, Zhuhong Zhang, and Shufen Mu, and earned her Ph.D. from the University of Pennsylvania under the supervision of Perry Link.

Patrick McAllister works in Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. He earned his doctorate at the University of Vienna (~2005–2011) under Helmut Krasser, Karin Preisendanz, and Ernst Steinkellner, and became a researcher at the Austrian Academy of Sciences around 2012.

Patrick Olivelle is an Indology and religious studies scholar. He studied at Oxford under Gombrich, Burrow, and Zaehner, and earned his Ph.D. at Penn under Ludo Rocher. He held posts at Indiana University Bloomington (1974–1991) and UT Austin (1991).

Patrick Pranke is a scholar in Buddhist studies, history, archaeology, and religious studies. He earned his Ph.D. at the University of Michigan (attested 2004) under the supervision of Luis Oscar Gómez and Victor B. Lieberman.
Patrick R. Uhlmann is a scholar in Buddhist studies who was a Ph.D. candidate at the University of California, Los Angeles, studying under Robert E. Buswell Jr. (attested 2012).

Patrul Rinpoche was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy. He studied under numerous teachers, including Jigme Gyelwai Nyugu (~1830–1842), Do Khyentse Yeshe Dorje (~1832), and Zhabkar Tsokdruk Rangdrol, and taught figures such as Shenphen Nangwa and Minyak Kunzang Sonam.

Paul B. Courtright is a scholar in Indology and religious studies. He held posts at the University of North Carolina at Greensboro and Emory University (attested 1998, 2026), where he is Professor Emeritus.

Paul B. Donnelly works in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Tibetology. He studied under Geshe Lhundup Sopa, Geshe Yeshe Thapkay, Losang Yarphel, and Lobsang Gyatso, and held a post at Northern Arizona University.

Paul Carus was a scholar of philosophy, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He studied at Greifswald, Strasbourg, and Tübingen (Ph.D. ~1874–1876), taught at Kriegsschule Dresden (~1876–1881), and edited for The Open Court and The Monist (~1887–1919).

Paul Copp specializes in Buddhist studies, Sinology, and religious studies. He studied at UMass Amherst and Princeton (Ph.D. attested 2005 under Stephen F. Teiser), and has held posts at Western Michigan University and the University of Chicago (attested 2014–2026).

Paul Crowe works in Sinology and religious studies. He completed graduate studies at the University of Calgary under Leslie S. Kawamura and Daniel L. Overmyer, and served as a professor at Simon Fraser University (attested 2010).

Paul David Devanandan was a religious studies scholar who earned a doctorate at Yale (~1927–1931). He taught at Jaffna College, served as professor at United Theological College, Bangalore (1932–1949), and directed the Christian Institute for the Study of Religion and Society (1956).

Paul David Numrich is a scholar of religious and Buddhist studies. He earned his doctorate from the University of Michigan (1992) and held faculty posts at Loyola University Chicago and the Theological Consortium of Greater Columbus (attested 2006).

Paul Debes was a Buddhist studies figure who founded the Buddhistisches Seminar (1948), the Buddhistische Gesellschaft Hamburg (1954), the journal Wissen und Wandel (1955), and the Deutsche Buddhistische Gesellschaft (1955).

Paul Demiéville was a Sinologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Sylvain Lévi and Paul Pelliot. He held posts at Xiamen University (1924–1926), INALCO (1931–1945), EPHE (1945–1957), and the Collège de France (1946–1964).

Paul Deussen was an Indologist and philosopher who studied under Christian Lassen at Bonn, Tübingen, and Berlin. He taught at RWTH Aachen University (~1876–1879), Berlin (1881–1887), and served as professor at Kiel University from 1889.
Paul Dundas was a scholar of Indology and religious studies. Educated at the University of Edinburgh, he served there as head of Asian studies (~1976–2017) and was also head of the Pali Text Society.

Paul E. Muller-Ortega is a scholar in Indology and religious studies who completed doctoral studies at the University of California, Santa Barbara. He held posts at Michigan State University (attested 1992) and the University of Rochester (attested 2000).
Paul Ekman studied at New York University (~1952–1954) and Adelphi University (~1954–1958). He held an academic post at the University of California, San Francisco, from approximately 1960 to 2004.
